items.headline: FMRB executive order T-minus-1 day: eighth witness (Treasury OCCIP Assistant Secretary) added; FTC Office of Technology + GAO Strategic Issues join requesting cohort; amicus coalition grows to sixteen organizations
items.diff_narrative: Yesterday entered the two-business-day window before the May 15 14:00 EDT classified threshold briefing with the witness slate at seven (Locascio plus ODNI cyber plus NSA Cyber plus MSTIC plus CISA Director plus FCC PSHSB Bureau Chief plus DOE CESER Assistant Secretary), the American Bar Association Cybersecurity Legal Task Force and the National Association of Attorneys General AI working group filed a joint Wednesday amicus letter joining the now-fourteen-organization coalition, and the House Energy and Commerce Subcommittee issued a Wednesday-afternoon follow-up press release confirming a coordinated request bundle with the Senate Cyber Subcommittee. Today enters the T-minus-1 window. Senate Cyber Subcommittee staff release a Thursday-morning final hearing-readiness memo locking the witness slate at eight with the addition of the Department of Treasury Office of Cybersecurity and Critical Infrastructure Protection Assistant Secretary, joining the previously-confirmed seven. The House Energy and Commerce Subcommittee issues a Thursday-morning press release confirming the parallel 30-day House technical review window now sits in joint-resolution drafting alongside the Senate Cyber Subcommittee staff. The Federal Trade Commission Office of Technology plus the Government Accountability Office Strategic Issues Team file a joint Thursday amicus letter joining the now-sixteen-organization coalition, narrowing focus to the per-state attorney-general consultation pathway plus the AISI cyber-evaluation reciprocity 120-day placement window alignment plus the new GAO independent-audit recommendation pathway. OSTP holds the Thursday-afternoon line that the executive order draft remains in interagency review with no signing window before May 22; the Senate Cyber Subcommittee confirms the May 15 briefing will proceed on schedule with the classified witness session opening at 14:00 EDT and the unclassified follow-on press briefing at 16:30 EDT.

items.headline: Indo-Pacific reciprocity perimeter reaches thirteen jurisdictions with UAE first formal Middle East entry; Saudi Arabia adjacent track; OECD GENAI ships attestation-field schema as draft Recommendation
items.diff_narrative: Yesterday Brazil's ANCiber published a Wednesday entry note converting open-ended observer interest into a formal exploratory-observer commitment with a 240-day national-consultation window, South Africa's Cybersecurity Hub plus the Department of Communications and Digital Technologies separately announced a parallel exploratory-observer track with a 270-day consultation window — the first African entry — and the OECD GENAI working-group secretariat published a Wednesday-afternoon procedural note describing the cohort as on track toward the first thirteen-jurisdiction formal mirror count by Q3 2026. Today the United Arab Emirates Cybersecurity Council and the Israel National Cyber Directorate jointly publish a Thursday-morning exploratory-observer commitment paired with a Saudi Arabia National Cybersecurity Authority Thursday-afternoon adjacent entry note signaling parallel exploratory-observer interest, citing the Wednesday Brazil plus South Africa precedent as the cross-continental procedural baseline; the UAE entry is the first Middle East formal entry into the cohort and the Saudi adjacent track marks the first GCC adjacent extension. The cohort now spans thirteen named candidates (Singapore, Japan, South Korea, New Zealand formally; Canada, Australia, India, Taiwan, Indonesia, Vietnam, Thailand, Brazil as observers; South Africa, UAE as exploratory observers; Saudi Arabia in adjacent-track pre-commitment) plus the originating UK and EU. The OECD GENAI working-group secretariat publishes a Thursday-afternoon procedural note formalizing the cyber-evaluation reciprocity attestation field schema as a draft Recommendation text with formal member-state circulation in the June 2-6 plenary window, citing the now-fourteen-jurisdiction cohort visibility as the operative procedural baseline.

items.headline: LangChain CVE-2026-44967 lands as tenth agent-checkpoint-and-manifest-loader CVE, extending the taxonomy to the intermediate-state-serializer sub-tier
items.diff_narrative: Yesterday AutoGen CVE-2026-44918 (CVSS 8.6) landed Wednesday-morning Pacific as the ninth CVE in the Trail of Bits taxonomy, a path-traversal vulnerability in the workflow-state checkpoint loader extending the taxonomy to the workflow-state path tier; the AutoGen maintainer team shipped v0.6.4 same-day, Trail of Bits published an addendum updating from eight to nine CVEs reaffirming the signed-checkpoint plus manifest-allowlist-validation plus workflow-state path-canonicalization three-tier mitigation pattern, and the DeepMind plus Meta AI plus Anthropic plus Microsoft Wednesday joint follow-up addendum v2 (arxiv 2605.06712v2) extended the runtime-verifier paper to the workflow-state tier. Today a fresh agentic-AI tooling-stack CVE drops at the intermediate-state-serializer sub-tier: LangChain CVE-2026-44967 (CVSS 8.8) is a path-traversal vulnerability in the workflow-state checkpoint loader's intermediate hand-off serializer that lets an attacker overwrite arbitrary host paths during cross-step state migration, mirroring the AutoGen CVE-2026-44918 Wednesday workflow-state pattern but at a finer-grained intermediate-state hand-off surface. The LangChain maintainer team ships v0.3.7 same-day with the patch plus a paired backport advisory for the v0.2.x and v0.1.x branches the NHS England blocklist references. Trail of Bits publishes a Thursday extended addendum updating its taxonomy from nine to ten agent-checkpoint-and-manifest-loader CVEs (adding LangChain workflow-state-intermediate), reaffirming the three-tier signed-checkpoint plus manifest-allowlist-validation plus workflow-state path-canonicalization common-mitigation pattern now extended with an intermediate-state-serializer canonicalization sub-pattern. DeepMind plus Meta AI plus Anthropic plus Microsoft co-publish a Thursday joint follow-up addendum v3 (arxiv 2605.06712v3) extending the Wednesday v2 paper with the intermediate-state serializer canonicalization formal-verification pattern; LangChain, AutoGen, CrewAI, and Pydantic AI publish Thursday parallel reaffirmation that the mid-June default-shipment commitment now covers all four tier-and-sub-tier surfaces.

items.headline: vLLM v0.11.4-rc1 ships signed-checkpoint loader as default closing parity gap with SGLang + TGI; throughput gap narrows to 4.3 percent — tightest of the benchmark cycle; Cloudflare Infire L40S reaches parity
items.diff_narrative: Yesterday SGLang RadixArk v0.5.7 and Hugging Face TGI v3.2.0 shipped Wednesday point releases adding a Sigstore-or-cosign-compatible signature-verified loader AND shipping it as the documented default load path for new installs — making SGLang the second open-source serving stack to ship the primitive AND the first to default it, and TGI the third; Yotta Labs placed the shared-prefix workload at 17,140 tok/s on vLLM v0.11.3 vs 18,860 tok/s on SGLang RadixArk v0.5.7 (gap holding 9.1 percent essentially flat); Cloudflare Infire L40S edge-tier advantage closed to 1.12x with parity projected at vLLM v0.11.4 Monday May 18. Today vLLM v0.11.4-rc1 ships a Thursday release-candidate adding the signature-verified model-checkpoint loader as the documented default for new installs (closing the parity gap with SGLang RadixArk plus TGI from Wednesday) plus shipping the intermediate-state-serializer canonicalization mitigation compatible with the Thursday LangChain CVE-2026-44967 disclosure; SGLang RadixArk v0.5.8 ships a Thursday point release adding the intermediate-state-serializer mitigation alongside its existing default signed-checkpoint loader; Hugging Face TGI v3.2.1 ships a parallel Thursday point release adding the intermediate-state-serializer mitigation. Yotta Labs places the shared-prefix workload at approximately 18,420 tok/s on vLLM v0.11.4-rc1 (up 7 percent from 17,140 Wednesday) versus 19,210 tok/s on SGLang RadixArk v0.5.8 (up 2 percent from 18,860 Wednesday) — the throughput gap narrows to 4.3 percent (vs 9.1 percent Wednesday), the tightest gap since the benchmark cycle began. Cloudflare Infire engineering reports that the v0.11.4-rc1 release-candidate plus the intermediate-state-serializer mitigation close the L40S edge-tier latency gap to parity (1.00x Infire-versus-vLLM ratio, vs 1.12x Wednesday), with parity arriving one trading session ahead of the previously-targeted Monday May 18 v0.11.4 stable release.

items.headline: Verifiable Intermediate-State-Serializer Canonicalization preprint covers ten-CVE pattern; runtime-verifier paper v3 extends mid-June framework target to intermediate-state sub-tier; Cross-Jurisdiction Reciprocity-Attestation companion paper ships
items.diff_narrative: Yesterday Verifiable Workflow-State Path Canonicalization for Agentic AI Multi-Tier Loaders (arxiv 2605.06799) shipped Wednesday as a fresh paper extending the runtime-verifier preprint plus the Tuesday inference-routing addendum to cover the workflow-state path tier exposed by the Wednesday AutoGen CVE-2026-44918 disclosure, with formal compositional safety theorems for the three-tier load-runtime-workflow loader pattern and Stanford CIS plus the Brennan Center adding as institutional reviewers; Runtime Signature-Verification v2 (arxiv 2605.06712v2) extended the Tuesday runtime-verifier paper with a workflow-state path-canonicalization integration pattern. Today opens a fresh research story-thread: Verifiable Intermediate-State-Serializer Canonicalization for Agentic AI Workflow-State Migration (arxiv 2605.06892) ships Thursday as a fresh paper extending the Wednesday workflow-state path-canonicalization paper to cover the intermediate-state hand-off serializer surface exposed by the Thursday LangChain CVE-2026-44967 disclosure; the paper provides formal compositional safety theorems for the four-tier-and-sub-tier load-runtime-workflow-state-intermediate-state loader pattern plus reference implementations in Python and Rust, with INRIA France and Tokyo Institute of Technology newly added to the institutional reviewer trajectory. Compositional Safety under Cross-Jurisdiction Reciprocity-Attestation Schemas (arxiv 2605.06934) ships Thursday as a companion paper extending the Tuesday cross-hemispheric composition verification work to cover the Thursday OECD GENAI cyber-evaluation reciprocity attestation field schema draft Recommendation text, providing compositional safety theorems for the now-fourteen-jurisdiction Indo-Pacific cohort tenant-policy field interop. Runtime Signature-Verification v3 (arxiv 2605.06712v3) extends the Wednesday v2 paper with an intermediate-state-serializer canonicalization integration pattern covering all ten CVE-pattern instances; Microsoft, LangChain, CrewAI, Pydantic AI, and AutoGen maintainer teams publish parallel Thursday commitments to ship the four-tier-and-sub-tier mitigation integration as a default in the next minor-version release, extending the coordinated mid-June default-shipment target to cover load-time signed-checkpoint plus runtime manifest-allowlist-validation plus workflow-state path-canonicalization plus intermediate-state-serializer canonicalization as a paired four-surface delivery.
